example_name: Task and Motion Planning with Obstacles
user_request_examples: Create a robot that picks blocks while avoiding obstacles
Set up a manipulation scene with walls that block direct paths
Build a task planner that works around obstacles
Make a robot stack blocks in constrained space
scenario_description: An iiwa14 robot must pick three blocks from the right side of a vertical wall obstacle and stack them in a designated zone on the left side. The wall divides the workspace, forcing the robot to plan trajectories that go over or around the obstacle. This demonstrates Task and Motion Planning (TAMP) where high-level task sequencing combines with low-level collision-free motion planning.

robot.reason: 7 DOF provides redundancy to navigate around obstacles

wall_obstacle.purpose: Forces robot to plan around obstacle

column_obstacle.purpose: Additional obstacle for path planning complexity

complexity_factors.task_planning: Determine sequence: which block to pick first, optimal stacking order
complexity_factors.workspace_constraints: Limited space due to wall and column
complexity_factors.stacking_precision: Blocks must be accurately stacked despite constrained approach
complexity_factors.redundancy_resolution: 7-DOF arm has multiple solutions; choose collision-free ones

step1_obstacle_modeling.wall: Static box blocking direct Y-axis motion
step1_obstacle_modeling.collision_geometry: Both obstacles have collision properties for contact detection

step2_task_planning.approach: Decide pick order and stacking sequence
considerations: Which block is easiest to reach?
task_sequence: Pick green block (easiest access at X=0.5, left edge)

strategy_1_over_wall.description: Lift block high and move over wall
strategy_1_over_wall.cons: Requires high reach, may exceed workspace

strategy_2_around_left.description: Move around left edge of wall (X < 0.3)
strategy_2_around_left.cons: Longer path, must avoid column at [0.4, -0.15]

strategy_3_around_right.description: Move around right edge of wall (X > 0.9)

for_each_block: Compute grasp configuration with collision-free IK
Compute place configuration with collision-free IK

step5_controller.waypoint_tracking: Switch target configuration when close to current waypoint

collision_avoidance_ik.purpose: Find configurations that maintain clearance from obstacles

redundancy_resolution.resolution: Use posture cost to prefer configurations away from obstacles
redundancy_resolution.cost: Quadratic cost on joint angles: minimize ||q - q_nominal||²

expected_behavior.phase_1: Pick green block from [0.5, 0.4], path goes around left edge (X < 0.3)
expected_behavior.phase_2: Place green block in stacking zone [0.6, 0.0, 0.435]
expected_behavior.phase_3: Pick blue block from [0.65, 0.4], similar path around obstacle
expected_behavior.result: Three blocks stacked in left zone, no collisions with obstacles

validation_criteria.collision_free: No collisions between robot and obstacles throughout execution
validation_criteria.successful_stacking: All three blocks stacked in target zone
validation_criteria.path_efficiency: Uses shortest collision-free path (around left edge)

ik_fails_near_obstacles.symptom: No IK solution found for grasp or place
solutions: Move stacking zone away from obstacles
Use smaller minimum distance threshold initially

collision_during_motion.symptom: Robot hits wall or column during trajectory
solutions: Sample trajectory more finely for collision checking
Trade off between clearance and path length

workspace_limits.symptom: Cannot reach around obstacles within workspace
solutions: Reposition robot base closer to center
Use over-wall strategy instead of around

extensions.sensor_based: Use depth camera to detect obstacles at runtime
